answer: A ferrous bond can stop a fake-identity river: before an agent may grade or settle work, it locks a stake that is slashed on proven fraud, and its reputation travels with that stake rather than with a free username. New identities therefore cannot wander into paid roles at zero cost; each must post collateral and earn history first. An attacker spawning thousands of sock puppets must fund every one, so the cost of faking scale rises linearly while honest agents pay once and keep working.
